title: L2 policy source + clause
description: Spec: CORPUS_DESIGN.md §3.3.2. One markdown file per policy document under L2-policy-clauses/; the file's front matter is a POLICY_SOURCE, each `## clause: <id>` section is a POLICY_CLAUSE. There is deliberately NO `source_text` field anywhere in this schema — gate G5.

source_id.description: `{platform}.{slug}` for a real source. The leading-underscore form is reserved for container records that hold no clauses of their own — `_stubs` is the only one (see `stub_entries`).

tier.description: A = public machine-readable CDN document; B = public HTML; C = public forum (never citable); D = login-gated, human-read only (N11); corroboration = third-party mirror, never citable.

marketplace_edition.description: The marketplace whose edition this document is, e.g. 'NA', 'US', 'IN', 'UK', 'unknown'. Drives jurisdiction_caveat.

content_sha256.description: Hash of the extracted text, not of the PDF bytes. Null on a stub.

citable.description: false for tier C and corroboration — gates G8 and G9. A non-citable source can inform an L3 pattern but can never reach a customer-facing citation.

jurisdiction_caveat.description: true where the document is a non-US edition or its edition could not be confirmed. Clauses from such a source are excluded from US drafting — gate G7.

stub.description: true where the document is known and named but its text could not be obtained through the proxy. A stub carries zero clauses. It is a recorded hole, never a fabricated summary.

reason_codes_covered.description: Every L1 code this source speaks to. Read by the loader (build.ts `reasonCodesCovered`) to route a source into a code's slice; declared here because gate G1 validates what the files actually carry, not a subset of it.

retrieval_note.description: How this document was obtained and what is uncertain about the edition. Free text a human wrote and a human reads; carried on the record so provenance travels with the source rather than living in a commit message.

stub_entries.description: Container-record only (`_stubs`): the named-but-unobtained sources. A recorded hole is a task; fabricating text to fill one is the one thing this corpus must never do. TWO FORMS ARE ACCEPTED FOR AN HONEST REASON: the L2 front-matter dialect (parse.ts) is deliberately FLAT — scalars and inline lists only — so a nested block authored in a `.md` file reaches every consumer as one opaque string, and today that is what this field is. The array form below is the shape it must take if any code is ever to read it; until then it is a human-readable record and no loader depends on it. Declaring only the array would make gate G1 fail forever on a file that is not wrong; declaring only the string would enshrine the limitation as the target.

our_summary.description: OUR PROSE, one entry per paragraph. This is the citation target (CORPUS_DESIGN §3.3.2 / §5.2): each paragraph becomes one content block in a custom-content document, so a citation resolves to (clause_id, block_index).

quoted_excerpt.description: Verbatim excerpt from the source, marked as an excerpt. Hard cap 25 words — gate G4 (CORPUS_DESIGN §3.6 copyright mitigation).
